---
title: "Fetching the data"
---

The third-party data this project depends on is 341 MB and belongs to the
people who produced it, so it is not in the repository.

```bash
pip install -e .
python -m gia_mip.data                         # both benchmarks, 24 MB
python -m gia_mip.data --collection giamip     # the GIAMIP inputs, 317 MB
python -m gia_mip.data --all
```

Every file is checked against the SHA-256 sum in
`gia_mip/resources/manifest.json` after download, so a fetched tree is known
to be the tree the conversions were made from. Archives are unpacked next to
themselves.

::: {.callout-important}
## Redistribution is not yet agreed

`python -m gia_mip.data` refuses to download any file whose `permission` is
not `granted`, and prints which one and why. At present that is every file.

The Spada and Martinec archives were supplied privately. The GIAMIP inputs
came through the project's own shared folder, and the ice histories are
re-gridded versions of third-party reconstructions that each carry their own
terms. Until each supplier has agreed, the files are obtained from the
supplier and placed in `data/original/` by hand, in the layout the manifest
describes.

[The manifest](manifest.qmd) records the permission state of every file.
:::

## Two axes

A file is addressed by the body of work it belongs to and by whether it is
untouched.

`--collection` takes `spada2011`, `martinec2018` or `giamip`, and `benchmarks`
as an alias for the first two. `--stage` takes `original` for an untouched
third-party file, the default, or `converted` for something this project
derived from one. The converted reference data is small and is tracked in the
repository under `data/converted/`, so the tests and the site build with no
network at all.

## Where the files go

The default destination is `data/` in the checkout, with `original/` and
`converted/` beneath it. Set `GIA_MIP_DATA_ROOT`, or pass `--dest`, to put
them somewhere else. On a machine with several worktrees, or on a cluster
where 341 MB does not belong in a checkout, point every worktree at one
directory.

An installed package has no checkout to fill, so `--dest` or
`GIA_MIP_DATA_ROOT` is required there and the fetcher says so instead of
writing into `site-packages`.

Archives are unpacked into a directory named after the archive, with the
archive's single top-level directory removed when it has one, so
`giamip/ice-history.zip` gives
`giamip/ice-history/iceHistory-ICE-6G_D.nc`. A stamp file inside the target
records which archive it came from, so a second run neither re-extracts
317 MB nor disturbs anything you put there.

## Checking what is there

```bash
python -m gia_mip.data --list           # what exists, and what is local
python -m gia_mip.data --verify --all   # re-check the sums, download nothing
```

`--verify` reports a file that is missing or whose sum has changed, and exits
non-zero. Run it after copying a tree between machines.
